review.summary: No remaining concrete reachable P0/P1/P2 blocker found in the bounded v2 fixes. The host-ID replay fix, Python exclusion, and one-shot skill preservation are source-verified and covered by inspected parent evidence. This is not live LLM, deployment, user-outcome, or data validation.

criterionResults.criterion: Run-local scope cannot authorize another frame, contract, actor, query or write, exceed its attempt budget, or survive restart/denial
criterionResults.observed: Every broker-facing scope and ordinary exact approval now receives a fresh host-generated ApprovalID; ToolCallID remains the provider/model ID only. Scope retains actor/frame/plan/budget checks, excludes Python, consumes before dispatch, and exact fallback rejects a mismatched resolved ApprovalID.
evidence: analysis_autonomy.go:19 uses crypto/rand.Text under the declared Go 1.26.5 toolchain; scope registration at :223 uses hostApprovalID while ToolCallID remains tc.ID, checks resolved.ApprovalID at :238, and records the host ID at :242.

loop.go:862-865 assigns a fresh host ID to scoped trace events; ordinary exact approval uses hostApprovalID at :879 and requires resolved.ApprovalID == approval.ApprovalID at :933. This closes both prior broker-cached scope replacement and exhausted-scope fallback replays.

analysis_autonomy_safety_test.go:16-61 simulates cached broker resolutions while reusing the model call ID across changed frame/budget proposals; analysis_autonomy_test.go:123-232 drives repeated provider IDs through Run, scope exhaustion, and exact fallback. Inspected rebuilt-v2.log reports pkg/agent, pkg/plugin, and pkg/mcp pass; review-regression-negative.log shows the old candidate fails these guards.

Existing run-local controls remain: successful-query-only frames at analysis_autonomy.go:157-181; org/user/session equality and pre-dispatch decrement at :250-280; new Run creates fresh autonomy state in loop.go:152.

criterionResults.criterion: Dynamic capability replacement stays inside existing permissions and current publication lifecycle, and replaces rather than accumulates skill context
criterionResults.observed: The reusable scope is deliberately narrowed to immutable-frame profile and exact-plan ML-contract execution; free-form Python stays on ordinary exact approval. Reselection can only draw from the pre-filtered catalog, skill context is per request, and one-shot requests retain then re-trim the selected skills. Publication continues to hide autonomy tools and preview completion closes tools/scope.
evidence: scopeTool and the tool schema allow only sandbox-analysis_profile_dataset and sandbox-analysis_execute_ml_contract (analysis_autonomy.go:35-41, :67-70); consumeScope permits Python neither in its tool switch nor allowed argument keys (:257-273), while ML requires contract_ref == the successful-frame plan (:259-264).

Run copies catalog only after RBAC/server-selection/exclusion filtering (loop.go:132-153); selectCapabilities admits only catalog entries (analysis_autonomy.go:119-132); publication omits local tools (analysis_autonomy.go:55-56) and successful preview clears openAITools and scope (loop.go:388-391).

loop.go:186 injects selected skills; :199-200 appends one-shot nudge to that already skill-injected request and re-trims it. analysis_autonomy_safety_test.go:69-99 checks truncation nudge preservation; updated loop_test.go:1266-1272 checks preview nudge preservation; analysis_autonomy_test.go:179-190 checks reselection/near-limit with a reused provider ID.
No new permission, data-query, write, publication, or tool-wide grant path was found in the reviewed changed blocks.

criterionResults.criterion: Tests and documentation accurately bound the delivered behavior without claiming live model or deployment validation
criterionResults.observed: The new tests target each prior finding, and the current design, embedded skills, default prompt, and settings-helper prompt all disclose the conservative Python boundary and no-live limitation. The prior first-batch document is explicitly historical and links to the new design.
evidence: analysis_autonomy_safety_test.go:16-67 covers cached-resolution replay, changed frame/budget, malformed extra field, budget limits, and Python ineligibility; analysis_autonomy_test.go:56-121 covers forged/failed frame, foreign session, plan mismatch, noncompute/query/write calls, exhaustion, fresh run, and denial/mismatched resolution.

The scoped Run seam at analysis_autonomy_test.go:123-232 asserts two scoped calls, a third independently rejected call, fresh non-provider approval IDs, and no skill accumulation. It labels its LLM/MCP fixtures as non-live.

docs/design/ask-o11y-bounded-autonomy.md:42-45 accurately explains why free-form Python remains exact-approved; :52-58 documents host-issued opaque IDs and broker replay rationale; :62-89 identifies local/mock evidence and negative old-candidate checks; :101-110 explicitly reserves deployment/live natural-language validation. docs/design/ask-o11y-autonomous-analyst.md:1-4 labels the earlier document historical. scripts/configure-ask-o11y-workflow-tools.py SYSTEM_PROMPT carries the same scope/Python limitation.

Inspected parent evidence rebuilt-v2.log records package passes and explicitly says 'not live LLM E2E'; review-regression-negative.log preserves failures against the old candidate. These were not executed by this reviewer.

residualRisks: No live LLM, Grafana deployment, approval-UI interaction, or production-data behavior was authorized or independently run; the design correctly leaves those as post-redeploy validation.

The crypto/rand host ID is probabilistic by design; no practical collision path was found, and its generated format is compatible with the previously inspected opaque approvalId UI/route/broker contract.
Reviewer performed no shell command or staged-file inspection under the read-only boundary; parent-owned rebuild/test logs were inspected as evidence only.

retrospective: Host-issued approval IDs, not model tool-call IDs, must key broker authorization decisions.
Same frame does not prove arbitrary Python honors an ML contract; keep free-form code exact-approved.
Inject replacement skills per request, and preserve them through every one-shot nudge path.
